title: No Coveting
kjv_text: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour's.
summary: Prohibits desiring what belongs to a neighbor — house, wife, servants, livestock. The Decalogue's only regulation of a mental state; also its plainest inventory of persons as property.
original_audience: Israelite householders; the 'neighbour' is a fellow covenant member, and the wife is listed among his assets.
immediate_context: Tenth commandment, closing the Decalogue by moving from act to appetite — the root of theft, adultery, and murder in one verse.
historical_context: Unique among ANE laws in criminalizing desire itself; no court could try it, which is precisely the point — it hands enforcement to conscience (or, in a theocracy, to whoever claims to audit conscience). The wife's placement between house and servants is Exhibit A for the property-status of women; Deuteronomy 5:21 pointedly re-orders to put her first and separate.
penalty: None stated; unenforceable by human courts by design.
cross_references: Joshua 7:21 (Achan: 'I coveted them, and took them')
nt_passages: Romans 7:7 — Paul says this commandment taught him what sin is
James 1:14-15 — desire conceiving sin conceiving death

internal_contradictions.issue: Is it OK to covet? The ban vs. Paul's 'covet earnestly the best gifts' (1 Cor 12:31) — same Greek verb in the Septuagint's register.
Does God approve of slavery? The verse lists servants as covetable property, presupposing the institution.

usofc_implementation: Unprosecutable, therefore perfect: the Covetousness Statute is the regime's universal pretext. Compliance runs through the NDS's Weekly Confession Assemblies, where citizens self-report desires; the confessions are logged. Advertising is regulated as 'incitement to covet,' giving the state a licensing chokehold on all marketing — the quietest, most total power in the Code.
constitutional_analogue: A pure thought-crime statute; the First Amendment and the entire liberal distinction between act and belief are its casualties. Its advertising arm inverts commercial speech doctrine.
scene_ideas: A confession assembly where a man admits coveting his neighbor's Sabbath Exemption License — and the log entry follows him for a decade.
An ad agency's Compliance Poet, whose job is selling a truck without inducing desire for the truck.
A detective who closes cases by pulling covetousness logs: everyone has confessed to wanting something someone else lost.
satirical_uses: The state's own propaganda organ runs recruitment ads promising 'the life your neighbor has' — cleared by a ruling that inciting covetousness toward the state is devotion.
